slo_title: Apply transform methods to practical engineering problems

mcq.q: \(\text{Find } F_c\left\{\frac{1}{4+x^2}\right\} \text{ using the known result } F_c\left\{\frac{1}{a^2+x^2}\right\} = \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{e^{-as}}{a}.\)
\(\text{Using the modulation property for Fourier cosine transform, if } F_c\{e^{-x}\} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{1}{1+s^2}, \text{ then } F_c\{e^{-x} \sin(2x)\} \text{ is:}\)
\(\text{Evaluate } \int_0^\infty \frac{dx}{(x^2+9)(x^2+16)} \text{ using Parseval's identity for Fourier cosine transforms with } f(x)=e^{-3x}, g(x)=e^{-4x}.\)
\(\text{Using the linearity property, find } F_c\{4e^{-3x} + 2e^{-x}\} \text{ given that } F_c\{e^{-ax}\} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{a}{s^2+a^2}.\)
\(\text{Given } F_s\{e^{-x}\} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \frac{s}{s^2+1}, \text{ find } F_s\{e^{-2x}\} \text{ using the scaling property.}\)

sq.q: \(\text{Using Fourier cosine transform, evaluate } \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{\cos(\lambda x)}{\lambda^2+a^2} d\lambda.\)
\(\text{Using Fourier sine transform, evaluate } \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{\lambda \sin(\lambda x)}{\lambda^2+a^2} d\lambda.\)

lq.q: \(\text{Find the Fourier sine transform of } f(x)=e^{-x}\sin(x).\)
answer: Step Marks \(F_s(s) = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-x} \sin(x) \sin(sx) dx\) (2) Use identity: \(\sin(x)\sin(sx) = \frac{1}{2}[\cos((1-s)x) - \cos((1+s)x)]\) (3) \(F_s(s) = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-x} [\cos((1-s)x) - \cos((1+s)x)] dx\) (3) Using formula: \(\int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-ax} \cos(bx) dx = \frac{a}{a^2 + b^2}\) (3) \(F_s(s) = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \left[ \frac{1}{1 + (1-s)^2} - \frac{1}{1 + (1+s)^2} \right]\) (4)
